hotspots.whyItMatters: Low-voltage licensing hinges on knowing which wiring rules (and which NEC article) apply to a given circuit type.
hotspots.cite: NTC Blue Book. Confirm chapter/section in your copy. Cross-check NEC Art. 725/760
hotspots.trap: Assuming every low-voltage circuit is automatically 'power-limited' just because the voltage is low. Power-limiting comes from the listed supply, not the voltage alone.

hotspots.whyItMatters: The exam distinguishes monitoring-service arrangements when asking about alarm system responsibilities.
hotspots.cite: NTC Blue Book. Confirm chapter/section in your copy
hotspots.trap: Treating 'monitored' as one single category instead of recognizing the different signal-transmission and response duties tied to each station type.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Battery standby duration requirements are a common low-voltage sizing question.
hotspots.cite: NTC Blue Book. Confirm chapter/section in your copy
hotspots.trap: Sizing standby battery capacity for quiescent (standby) current only and forgetting to add the alarm-condition current draw for the required alarm period.
